factors.value_notes: Partly sourced. The 2016 ASMFC benchmark assessment reports weakfish in shallow marine/estuarine waters at about 17–26.5°C and describes seasonal migration associated with the 16–24°C isotherms; this overlaps the configured 16–24°C ideal interval but describes observed habitat and migration, not a validated thermal optimum. A NOAA technical report describes a small adult aquarium study acclimated at 19–20°C; gradual warming toward 29°C initially increased activity consistent with avoidance, followed by acclimation. That experiment does not establish 29°C as preferred. Geographic identity is a major caveat: ASMFC documents Florida Atlantic Coast hybridization with sand seatrout and reports pure weakfish are rare southward; VIMS describes Florida occurrence as uncommon. Do not interpret this broad coastal evidence as a South Florida local abundance or catch curve.
